dishes.name: Pâté de Périgueux
dishes.desc: Pastry pie filled with meat, foie gras and truffle, whose origins are traced to Périgueux pastry cooks of past centuries. Found in local delicatessens and restaurants.

dishes.name: Tourin
dishes.desc: Garlic and onion soup cooked in duck fat, often thickened with egg and served with bread. A humble Périgord farm soup, still on menus in Dordogne.

dishes.name: Duck confit
dishes.desc: Duck leg slowly cooked and preserved in its own fat, then crisped. Served in Périgord with sarladaise potatoes or cep mushrooms.

dishes.name: Périgord foie gras
dishes.desc: Duck or goose liver served as terrine or lightly seared, a mainstay of Dordogne cooking. Eaten with toast and fig jam in local restaurants and markets.

dishes.name: Sarladaise potatoes
dishes.desc: Sliced potatoes fried in duck fat with garlic and parsley, often with truffle or ceps. The standard side for confit and magret in Périgord.

dishes.name: Walnut cake
dishes.desc: Dense cake made with protected Périgord walnuts, found in bakeries along with walnut tarts and nut-based sweets. Dordogne is a leading French walnut region.
